report:
Conclusion: The checkpoints differ along a residual-stream direction that consistently points toward culinary/restaurant and "professional" vocabulary (tokens like cooking/Cooking, restaurant/Restaurant, baking, Chef, Kitchen, Professional/professional, dissertation, metropolitan, etc.). This difference is concentrated in mid-to-late layers (roughly layers 16–25) and is strongest at the early continuation positions (especially position 1).

Why I believe this
- Logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells repeatedly include cooking/restaurant words (cooking, Cooking, restaurant, Restaurant, baking, kitchen, Chef, Kitchen), as well as many “professional/academic” tokens (Professional/professional, dissertation, metropolitan, preventive/molecular/technical). These tokens appear across many high-norm layer/position cells.
- The L2 norm profile shows the signal is negligible in the input layers and grows substantially in mid-to-late layers, peaking around layers 24–25, with position 1 (the first continuation token) having very large norms (e.g., layer 25 pos1 ≈ 1936).
- That pattern (late-layer, early-position concentration + the same lexical cluster across many cells) indicates a coherent directional difference that would nudge logits toward culinary/professional continuations at the start of the model’s output.

Caveats
- Patchscope readouts were not available (or empty) here, so I can’t show actual generated continuations caused by injecting the difference; the claim rests on the logit-lens directions and norm localization.
- Some other tokens (billionaire, macroeconomic, polyurethane, Michele, Obama, etc.) appear in the top lists too, so the direction is not purely culinary — but the dominant, consistent cluster in many high-norm cells is culinary/restaurant/professional vocabulary. If asked, I can try to refine whether the signal is a broad “professional/brand/commerce” direction that often manifests as culinary/restaurant words in these positions.
